headline: Tumor survival, subtype and treatment response predicted from single-omic, incomplete or inferred molecular layers
label: Oncology Multi Omic Survival Modeling
summary: Seven oncology items span survival, subtyping and drug-response models that use partial or inferred molecular layers, including bulk deconvolution and missing modalities.
synthesis: The items converge on predicting clinical phenotypes in TCGA-centered cancer data when the available molecular information is partial, single-layer, or inferred. DMG-PoE addresses missing modalities with a dynamic modality graph and product-of-experts fusion, while CMVAE aligns single-omic latent spaces with survival through contrastive supervision. DeSCENT derives reference-informed cellular profiles from bulk RNA-seq, and Genialis infers tumor immune state to predict immunotherapy response comparably to outcome-trained models. MODAE+ transfers cell-line drug response to tumours, GOTSurv uses unbalanced optimal transport for risk strata and progression routes, and HHRM classifies hierarchical subtypes with SHAP-based interpretation. The shift from the prior cross-layer inference emphasis is toward clinically oriented oncology endpoints, with no foundation-model reuse in these items.
